subject: Culture
title: Bastille Day
description: A quick, practical guide to Bastille Day.

hook.text: On July 14, 1789, a Paris mob stormed a prison holding just seven inmates. It changed the world.

buildup.text: The Bastille symbolized royal tyranny. Its fall became the opening act of the French Revolution.

discovery.text: France didn't officially celebrate Bastille Day until 1880—nearly a century after the event.

twist.text: The holiday actually honors a peaceful 1790 unity festival, not the violent storming. Lawmakers chose the calmer date.

climax.text: Nations pick their founding myths carefully. The symbol matters more than what actually happened.

punchline.text: The revolution began with a mostly empty prison.

quiz.question: How many prisoners were actually held in the Bastille when it was stormed?
